reported_mineral_classes.evidence: MRO/CRISM mafic absorptions at the descent-stage crash site are compatible with olivine and/or pyroxene, but do not distinguish them; published rover soil diffraction supports a basaltic pyroxene component.
MRO/CRISM crash-site spectrum is consistent with possible olivine and/or pyroxene. An olivine-enriched barchan-dune CRISM sample lies outside the 5km window but inside the 10km window.
MRO/CRISM 2.2-micrometre absorption in light-toned fractured material is interpreted as hydroxylated silica; published sample centre lies outside the 5km detailed window.

published_observations.interpretation: Dust-cleared basaltic substrate; no unique orbital mineral identification at this exact sample.
Mafic absorptions consistent with olivine and/or pyroxene; spectral bands do not permit unique mineral identification.
2.2-micrometre absorption consistent with hydroxylated silica, interpreted from orbital spectral data.
Relative high-calcium-pyroxene spectral enrichment in a dune sample, not a site-wide mineral fraction.
Relative olivine spectral enrichment in a barchan-dune sample, not a site-wide mineral fraction.

source.dataset: Seelos et al. (2014), Mineralogy of the MSL Curiosity landing site in Gale crater as observed by MRO/CRISM

secondary_source.dataset: Sautter et al. (2014), Igneous mineralogy at Bradbury Rise: the first ChemCam campaign at Gale crater

source.instrument: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CRISM; Curiosity surface measurements for context

methods.area: No mineral-class polygons or raster classification available; mapped_fraction=0 denotes unavailable mapped coverage, not mineral absence.
methods.literature_extraction: Named mineral classes are transcribed from published CRISM spectral interpretations near Bradbury Landing, with source sample locations and locality flags.
methods.location_test: Sample coordinate offsets tested against 5km and 10km projected square extents using Mars equirectangular projection with R=3396190m; distance approximated in this same projection.
methods.caveat: Qualitative mineral evidence does not imply unique mineral identification at all points, abundance, or area fraction. Some published source samples are outside the 5km detailed site.
methods.stage2_scoring: Do not treat literature-supported classes as mapped coverage fractions or score against Earth polygon-area mineral fractions.
